topics.title: Why some features cost money
topics.summary: Open source, no ads, and cloud work priced at cost.

blocks.text: opencast is free and open source, with no ads and no tracking. Almost everything runs on your device: playback, downloads, Whisper transcription, on-device ad detection, and iCloud sync through your own account.
What costs money

Cloud transcription runs on Cloudflare Workers AI and uses **transcription credits**. From version 2026.11.1 it is the only feature that does: ad detection and Chapters & Summary run on your device and call Google Gemini or OpenAI with an API key you add in Settings › AI Services, so your provider bills your own account. Until January 1, 2027 they also work without a key; after that, every install keeps five free analyses, then asks for one. In versions before 2026.11.1, ad detection and Chapters & Summary use Google's Gemini models through opencast's own services, and Chapters & Summary uses credits.

items: Credits come in two one-time packs, 20 hours and 100 hours. There are no subscriptions and nothing renews.
Prices cover the server cost plus Apple's commission, with a small buffer for failed jobs. They are not a profit center.
Packs are currently sold in the United States App Store only.

blocks.title: What leaves your device
blocks.text: A cloud transcription job receives only that episode's audio. Ad detection and Chapters & Summary receive only the transcript text, sometimes with the episode and show titles, never the audio. With your own key, transcript text goes from your device to the provider you chose. During the free analyses it passes through opencast's trial service, which adds opencast's key and stores none of it. Your subscriptions, listening history, and account details stay on your device.

topics.title: How credits work
topics.summary: Hours are estimated before a job and settled when it finishes.

blocks.text: Credits are measured in audio hours. Buy a pack from Settings › Credits and the hours are added to the balance tied to your App Store account.
What each job costs

items: Cloud transcription (Cloudflare Workers AI) charges the episode's length.
Cloud ad detection charges the episode's length and delivers the transcript too.

blocks.text: From version 2026.11.1, Chapters & Summary uses your own API key instead of credits; in versions before 2026.11.1, it uses about 2.2 hours of credit per hour of episode.
The estimated charge is shown before a job starts. A job can run slightly past your balance; the shortfall appears as **Owed** and comes out of your next pack.
Every App Store account receives one free hour, once, the first time opencast verifies it.

blocks.title: Balance looks wrong?
blocks.text: Use Refresh Purchases on the Credits screen. Purchases follow your App Store account, so reinstalling the app or changing iCloud settings does not affect them.
Refunds are handled by Apple. Choose Request a Refund on the Credits screen to open Apple's refund form for a purchase.

topics.title: Voice Boost
topics.summary: Lifts quiet voices and evens out volume.

blocks.text: Voice Boost lifts quiet speech and evens out volume swings, so a show recorded at low levels or with unevenly miked guests stays comfortable at one volume setting.

items: **Always** applies it to every episode.
**Per Episode** lets you turn it on or off from Now Playing for the episode you're listening to.
**Off** plays the original audio untouched.

blocks.text: Processing happens on your device in real time and never changes the downloaded file.

topics.title: Ad detection
topics.summary: Find promo and ad breaks on your device or in the cloud.

blocks.text: Detect Ads transcribes an episode and marks the promo and ad breaks. With Auto-Skip on, playback jumps over them. With it off, the breaks stay visible in Now Playing so you can skip them by hand.
Where it runs

items: **On This Device** transcribes on your device and uses no credits. On iPhone it uses Whisper's **Fast** model. On an iPad that can transcribe in the background, it uses Apple transcription when the show's language is supported, and Whisper otherwise. **Use Apple Transcription** doesn't change this.

**In the Cloud** has opencast's transcription service run Whisper on Cloudflare Workers AI and charges transcription hours. It fetches the audio from the podcast's host, and your device uploads its copy only when the two differ. It is faster and delivers the transcript too.
**Ask First Time** shows this choice the first time you tap Detect Ads on an episode.

blocks.text: From version 2026.11.1, in both modes your device sends the transcript text to Google Gemini or OpenAI with the API key you add in Settings › AI Services, and opencast's servers are not in that path. Without a key it goes through opencast's trial service, which adds opencast's Google key and stores none of the text: until January 1, 2027 with no limit per install, then for five free analyses per install. In versions before 2026.11.1, the transcript text is sent to opencast's ad-analysis service, which uses Google's Gemini models to find the breaks. The audio itself never leaves your device unless you chose the cloud option.
Automatic skips apply only when the downloaded audio matches the analyzed transcript, so a re-edited episode never skips at the wrong spot.

topics.title: Using your own API key
topics.summary: Ad detection and Chapters & Summary on your own Google or OpenAI account.

blocks.text: Ad detection and Chapters & Summary run on your device and call the AI provider whose key you add in **Settings › AI Services**: Google Gemini or OpenAI. Your device sends the transcript text straight to that provider, sometimes with the episode and show titles, never the audio, and opencast never sees your key. Recap and Ask use Apple's Private Cloud Compute and need no key.
Getting a key

items: **Google Gemini**: create a key in Google AI Studio. A Gemini key is free to create.
**OpenAI**: create a key on the API keys page of your OpenAI account. OpenAI bills API use to that account.
In Settings › AI Services, open the provider, paste the key, tap **Test** to check it, then **Save**.
With keys for both providers, choose which one each feature uses under **Provider**.

blocks.text: What it costs

Your provider bills your own account at its API prices; opencast charges nothing for these features. Google's free tier costs nothing within its limits, which are low: opencast slows down to stay inside the per-minute limit, so a long episode takes longer, and a key that reaches its daily limit can't run another analysis until the limit resets. Settings › AI Services shows the tokens each run used, counted on your device. Your provider's dashboard is the bill.
Your key on your devices

items: With **Sync with iCloud Keychain** on, the default, the key is saved in your iCloud Keychain and works on your other devices that use iCloud Keychain.
With it off, the key stays on this device only. Turning sync off for a synced key keeps it here and removes the synced copy from your other devices.
A key kept on this device only is the one used here, even when a synced key also exists. If you remove it, a synced key from another device can still be used here.
When a synced copy is also on your other devices beside this device's own key, the key screen offers **Remove synced copy**, which removes it from your other devices and keeps the key here.

blocks.text: Removing a key

Open the provider in Settings › AI Services and choose **Remove Key**. When a synced copy exists, removing the key deletes it everywhere: on this device and on your other devices that use iCloud Keychain. **Delete Data** doesn't remove your keys, and keys stay in the Keychain after you delete the app, so remove them here when you no longer want them.
Free analyses

Without a key, ad detection and Chapters & Summary go through opencast's trial service, which adds opencast's own Google key. Until January 1, 2027 they work without a key. After that, every install keeps five free analyses across both features, then asks for a key. One analysis is one Detect Ads or Chapters & Summary run on one episode, and a run that picks up again after an interruption doesn't count twice.
Privacy

items: **Google Gemini**: on Google's free tier, Google may use what you send and its answers to improve its products, and human reviewers may read them. With a paid Gemini key, Google doesn't use your prompts or responses to improve its products, and logs them for a limited period only to detect abuse and meet legal requirements.
**OpenAI**: OpenAI doesn't use API data to train its models unless you opt in, and keeps abuse-monitoring logs for up to 30 days.

**Free analyses**: the trial service holds the text in memory only for the request and stores no results. To count free analyses it keeps this install's App Attest key and, under one-way hashes, how many free analyses the install has used and each run's feature, times, token counts and cost, plus daily and monthly totals that carry no identifier; Google does not use trial requests to improve its products.

topics.title: Transcription engines
topics.summary: Whisper works everywhere; Apple transcription on supported devices.

blocks.text: Transcripts power transcript search, ad detection, and Chapters & Summary. They are generated on your device unless you choose a cloud job.
Whisper

**Fast** uses a small English-only model (about 50 MB) that keeps transcription quick. **Accurate** downloads the large-v3 model (about 600 MB) for better results at the cost of speed and battery. Either model is stored on this device and can be deleted from Settings › Transcription.
Apple transcription

On supported devices, **Use Apple Transcription** in Settings › Transcription makes **Generate Transcript** use Apple's on-device speech engine. It runs only while opencast is open in the foreground and starts over if the app is closed, backgrounded, or the screen locks mid-transcript. **Improve Transcript** works the same way. With the switch off, Generate Transcript uses Whisper, keeps running in the background, and can resume where it stopped. When a language or device isn't supported, Whisper is used automatically. Detect Ads picks its own engine (see Ad detection).
Cloud transcription

Transcribe Remotely and cloud ad detection have opencast's transcription service run Whisper on Cloudflare Workers AI. It fetches the audio from the podcast's host, and your device uploads its own copy only when the two differ. They use transcription credits and are the only way audio leaves your device.

topics.title: Recap and Ask
topics.summary: Summaries and answers from an episode's transcript, on Apple Intelligence.

blocks.text: **Recap** and **Ask** are in the transcript's **Transcript Options** menu once an episode has a transcript, on devices that support Apple Intelligence. Recap summarizes the last five minutes or everything so far; Ask answers questions about the episode, with citations you can tap to jump to that moment.

blocks.title: Where the passages go
blocks.text: Passages from this episode's transcript are sent to Apple's Private Cloud Compute to answer. Apple does not store them. Your audio is never sent. Results stay on this device. No opencast server is involved, and neither feature uses transcription minutes.

items: Apple's model may decline a passage. opencast shows a short notice, does not retry, and an Ask conversation keeps going.
Recaps are cached on this device so a repeat tap answers at once; Ask conversations are not saved. **Delete Data** clears the cache and the one-time notice.
Nothing runs until you tap Recap or Ask. Turning off Apple Intelligence in iOS Settings stops both.
Neither feature needs an API key.

topics.title: Make a Playlist with Apple Intelligence
topics.summary: Playlists drafted from one show's episode list, on Apple Intelligence.

blocks.text: **Make a Playlist** drafts playlists from one show's episodes, for a request you type or as suggested groups, and you choose which ones to save. On a show's page, open the **Podcast Actions** menu, or open the Playlists screen's **Add** menu, and choose **Make a Playlist…** under **Apple Intelligence · Beta**; from the Playlists screen you then pick the show. It appears on devices that support Apple Intelligence, for shows with at least three episodes.
Using it

items: Describe the playlist you want in your own words and tap **Ask**, or tap **Suggest Groups** to have it propose groups by topic, series, or story arc. On a long show, suggestions look at the newest 150 episodes.

Nothing is saved until you choose. Rename a draft, swipe an episode to remove it, use **Edit** to reorder, or open the draft's options menu to sort it **Oldest First** or **Newest First** or remove the whole playlist.
**Add Episodes…** lists the show's other episodes, best matches first, so you can add ones the draft missed.
**Save** keeps the drafts as ordinary playlists. **Cancel** asks before it discards them.

blocks.title: What is sent
blocks.text: This show's name, its episode titles, dates, lengths and short descriptions, and your request are sent to Apple's Private Cloud Compute to answer. On a long show only part of the list may be sent: the episodes that best match your request, or the newest ones that fit. Your audio, transcripts, feed address, and listening history are never sent; Apple does not store any of it, and no opencast server is involved. Try a Simpler Answer sends the same kinds of details and asks the model for episode numbers only.

Make a Playlist is labelled Beta. Apple's model may decline a request; opencast tries once more before telling you, and you can then try again or choose **Try a Simpler Answer**, an experimental retry that asks only for episode numbers and names the playlists on your device. Results may vary. It uses the same Apple Intelligence allowance as Recap and Ask, with nothing to buy and no API key, and turning off Apple Intelligence in iOS Settings stops it.

topics.title: iCloud sync
topics.summary: Subscriptions, listening progress, and playlists follow your Apple account.

blocks.text: With iCloud on, your subscriptions, listening progress, and playlists sync between your devices through your own iCloud account. opencast has no server in the middle and never sees them.

items: Downloads, transcripts, caches, and settings stay on each device.
A smart playlist's **Downloaded Only** rule reads each device's own downloads.
If iCloud is off or unavailable, everything keeps working locally on this device.
If sync ever leaves duplicate entries behind, Settings › Diagnostics › Repair Sync Duplicates merges them.

topics.title: Storage
topics.summary: Automatic caches are capped; downloads follow your limits.

blocks.text: opencast keeps two automatic caches: feed data (up to 128 MB) and artwork (up to 256 MB). When a cache goes over budget, the least recently used files are removed. Clear Automatic Caches empties both; nothing you chose to keep is affected.

Downloaded episodes stay until you delete them, unless a limit removes them. Keep Downloaded, set for every show in Download Settings (the gear in Downloads) or for one show in its own download settings, keeps only a show's most recently downloaded episodes; when it has more, the oldest are removed. Delete Downloads After Played removes episodes once they're played. Neither removes the current episode, or an episode being transcribed or scanned for ads.

A show set to Download New Episodes downloads its newest episode right away, then each new episode when the show refreshes while opencast is open, up to its limit at a time (three with No Limit). With Wi-Fi Only for Automatic Downloads on, these wait for Wi-Fi: on cellular or in Low Data Mode nothing is lost, they start on the next Wi-Fi refresh. Episodes you download yourself use any connection.
Delete All Downloads removes the files but keeps your subscriptions and listening progress.

Whisper models are managed from Settings › Transcription. Delete Data removes your library, listening progress, downloads, transcripts, analyses, caches, downloaded models, and settings from this device and, from version 2026.11.1, asks every opencast service this app uses to forget this install (earlier versions told only the notification service). If a service can't be reached, the next Delete Data asks again. Your own AI keys stay, and the free-trial count is not reset.

topics.title: Notifications
topics.summary: New-episode alerts from opencast's own service.

blocks.text: New Episode Notifications are sent by opencast's own notification service, not by a third party. It checks the feeds you follow and sends a push when a new episode appears.

To do that it stores a push token for this device and the list of feeds you follow, tied to an anonymous install identity. Turning notifications off disables the token, and Delete Data removes the install entirely.

items: If iOS permission was denied, use Open Settings to allow notifications for opencast.
Delivery depends on how often the publisher updates its feed and on the service's polling schedule.

topics.title: Siri
topics.summary: Say “in opencast” so Siri picks the right app.

blocks.text: opencast shares your shows with Siri so you can ask for them by name. Include “in opencast” so Siri knows which podcast app to use.

items: “Play Security Now in opencast”
“Resume my podcast in opencast”
“Play at double speed in opencast”

topics.title: Share an Episode
topics.summary: Send a link that plays in any browser, from the start or from where you are.

blocks.text: **Share Episode** is in the **Episode Actions** menu on an episode's page, in the menu you get by touching and holding an episode in a list, and in **More Actions** in Now Playing. It sends a link to a web player at opencast.mobile that plays the episode in any browser, with no app or account needed.

items: Once you've started an episode, choose **Share**, then **Share from 12:34** to start the listener where you are. While it's playing, the choice reads **Share from Current Time** and starts wherever playback is when you send it.
In Messages, the link shows the episode's artwork with a Play button, so it can play right in the conversation.
The web player has play and pause, skip back and forward, playback speed, and a **Download** button that saves the audio file.

blocks.title: What the link contains
blocks.text: The link itself holds the episode's audio address, titles, artwork, feed address, and date. Nothing about you or your library is in it, and nothing is stored on a server, so a link can't be recalled once you've sent it. The audio and artwork load from the podcast's own host, just as in any podcast app.
